name: The Hanged Man
upright: Change made deliberately: hardened baselines, and every change requested, reviewed, approved, tested and documented.
reversed: Untested patches rushed into production, settings drifting unseen, and emergency fixes no one ever writes down.
vision: A calm figure hangs upside down by one foot from a living T-shaped tree. Every branch is grown from cuttings of one blessed mother branch. At dawn a gardener traces the tree in chalk and snips any twig that strays past the line, though no one asked it to grow. A council of crows on the crossbar must hear, debate and vote on the smallest twitch of the figure's toe, rehearse it on a straw dummy, choose an hour and write it in a ledger. When lightning splits a branch, the figure splints it alone; at sunrise the crows still inspect and record the splint. The halo sweeps the bark, lighting every crack fresh sap has not sealed.
decode: Every branch grown from cuttings of one mother branch → imaging: systems built from one hardened, approved golden image start from the same secure baseline.
The chalk outline; stray twigs nobody asked for, snipped → drift detection: a setting changed with no change request is unauthorized; flag it and restore the baseline.
The council of crows that hears, votes, rehearses, picks an hour and writes it down → the CAB: request, review, approve or reject, test, schedule and implement, document.
The splint made alone, inspected and recorded at sunrise → an emergency change may skip prior approval, but it is still reviewed and documented afterward.
The halo lighting every unsealed crack → vulnerability scans find missing patches and misconfigurations; credentialed scans see far more than uncredentialed ones.
facts: Patch management order: evaluate, test, approve, deploy, verify. Test on systems that mirror production; verification proves each patch actually landed.
When an actively exploited zero-day has no patch, apply compensating controls: disable or isolate the service, block the attack vector and watch it closely.
Configuration management sets and records baselines; change management controls every later modification, and each approved change updates the documented baseline.
trap: The collective's oldest scar: an urgent patch pushed straight into production that caused the very outage it was meant to prevent. Urgency shortens the queue; it never skips the test.
